name: SignalPeople
title: Signal People
description: Save and find the people the organisation engages, prospects and customers, in Signal.
whenToUse: Pick to keep a record of a person the organisation is engaging: save what was found about them, find a person already held, or list the organisation's prospects and customers. Signal finds a person again by their LinkedIn, email or app account, so saving twice updates rather than duplicates. Attach it via a service edge to an agent node, or wire it in sequence to list everyone Signal holds with no agent, such as to fill a page.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: Trigger to fire the node. Carries no data; the organisation is the run's own.

outputs.name: people
outputs.description: Everyone Signal holds, newest first: person_id, name, role, company, stage, email, linkedin, crm_provider, observed, understood, inferred, researched, created_at, updated_at

stage.title: Stage
stage.description: Only people at this stage, prospect or customer. Leave empty for everyone.

limit.title: How many
limit.description: The most people to return, newest first. Leave empty for the service's own cap.

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller's account must carry, as noun:verb (finance:approve, payments:refund). Leave blank to require only that they are signed in.

package.name: signal
package.packageFile:
# SIGNAL — who a person is and what happens next (docs/architecture/signal/README.md). Signal
# holds everyone the organisation engages, prospects and customers, one record per person per org
# (SIGNAL.md § 4a, ruled 2026-10-09). The record is the memory service's; these nodes reach it
# through the engine at loopback, as the dataset package does, so no node knows its address.
name: signal
displayName: Signal
description: Save and read the people the organisation engages, prospects and customers
version: 0.1.0
category: storage
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751366180/gravity/icons/gravityIcon.png

features:
  - Save one person, found again by their LinkedIn, their email or their app account, never made twice
  - Find one person, and list the organisation's prospects and customers, as an Agent's tools
  - Keep what research found about them in Signal's layers (observed, understood, inferred)
  - Open and keep an Agent's own goals for a person, never another's, without reading anyone

allowedHosts:
  - 127.0.0.1

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.6.0"
  transport: [json]

shared.schema.yaml:
# TOOL DISCOVERY, as DATA: what an attached Agent reads before saving or finding a person. The
# wording IS the routing: a model reads these descriptions when choosing a tool, so rephrasing is a
# behaviour change, never a tidy-up. The argument shapes are what the model fills in.

people:
  name: Signal People
  version: "0.1.0"
  description: Save and find the people the organisation engages, in Signal, its own record of them.
  instructions: |-
    SIGNAL PEOPLE PROTOCOL:
    - save_person needs at least one way to recognise the person: linkedin, email or user_id.
      It finds the person already held by those, strongest first, and updates them, or makes them.
    - Only what you pass is written; anything left out keeps its old value. Each layer you pass
      (observed, understood, inferred, researched) replaces that layer whole.
    - Never pass a value you were not given or did not find. Leave it out rather than guess.
    - Whether a person is a prospect or a customer is Signal's to decide, never yours.
    - A tool that answers ok: false carries the reason. Say so rather than claiming it was saved.
  methods:
    save_person:
      description: >-
        Save one person to Signal: find them by their LinkedIn, email or app account and update
        them, or make them. Returns the person as now held, with their id, and whether they are new.
      input:
        type: object
        properties:
          linkedin:
            type: string
            description: Their LinkedIn profile URL or handle.
          email:
            type: string
            description: Their email address.
          user_id:
            type: string
            description: Their app account id, when they have signed in.
          name:
            type: string
            description: Their full name.
          company:
            type: string
            description: The company they work for now.
          role:
            type: string
            description: Their role there.
          crm_provider:
            type: string
            description: The CRM that also holds them, such as hubspot.
          crm_id:
            type: string
            description: Their record's id in that CRM.
          observed:
            type: object
            description: >-
              Facts found about them: location, the company's domain and website, their email and
              what it rests on (emailBasis), their pictures each with the page it came from, their
              employers with dates, and the news that names them.
            properties:
              location: { type: string, description: Where they are based. }
              domain: { type: string, description: Their company's web domain. }
              website: { type: string, description: Their company's website address. }
              emailBasis: { type: string, description: What their email address rests on. }
              pictures:
                type: array
                description: Pictures of them, their profile photo first.
                items:
                  type: object
                  properties:
                    url: { type: string, description: The picture's own address. }
                    page: { type: string, description: The page it came from. }
              employers:
                type: array
                description: Their employers, latest first.
                items:
                  type: object
                  properties:
                    company: { type: string }
                    role: { type: string }
                    from: { type: string, description: When they started, as found. }
                    to: { type: string, description: When they left; empty while they are there. }
              inTheNews:
                type: array
                description: News that names them, latest first.
                items:
                  type: object
                  properties:
                    title: { type: string, description: The story's headline. }
                    what: { type: string, description: What the story says of them, in a line. }
                    source: { type: string, description: The publication. }
                    date: { type: string }
                    url: { type: string }
          understood:
            type: object
            description: >-
              What has been learned: what they care about (each point with its exact quote, date
              and link), how they decide, where they have spoken (title, kind, date, link), what is
              live at their company.
            properties:
              whatTheyCareAbout:
                type: array
                description: What they care about, each point with their exact words.
                items:
                  type: object
                  properties:
                    point: { type: string, description: The point, in a few words. }
                    quote: { type: string, description: Their exact words. }
                    date: { type: string }
                    url: { type: string, description: Where they said it. }
              howTheyDecide:
                type: array
                description: How they decide, one line each.
                items: { type: string }
              spokenAt:
                type: array
                description: Where they have spoken.
                items:
                  type: object
                  properties:
                    title: { type: string }
                    kind: { type: string, description: A talk, a podcast, a panel, an interview. }
                    date: { type: string }
                    url: { type: string }
              companyNow:
                type: array
                description: What is live at their company now.
                items:
                  type: object
                  properties:
                    headline: { type: string }
                    date: { type: string }
                    url: { type: string }
          inferred:
            type: object
            description: >-
              What follows from it: why they would want what the organisation offers (whyUs: the
              reason, the quote it rests on, the part of the offer that answers it), the questions
              to ask, what to avoid.
            properties:
              whyUs:
                type: object
                description: Why they would want what the organisation offers.
                properties:
                  reason: { type: string, description: The reason, in a sentence. }
                  quote: { type: string, description: Their exact words it rests on. }
                  quoteUrl: { type: string, description: Where they said it. }
                  partOfOffer: { type: string, description: The part of what the organisation offers that answers it. }
              questions:
                type: array
                description: The questions to ask them.
                items: { type: string }
              whatToAvoid:
                type: array
                description: What to avoid with them.
                items: { type: string }
          researched:
            type: object
            description: The sources used and how sure the identity is.
            properties:
              sources:
                type: array
                description: The address of every source used.
                items: { type: string }
              confidence: { type: string, description: How sure the identity is, and why. }
    find_person:
      description: >-
        Find one person Signal holds, by their id, LinkedIn, email or app account. Returns
        found false when Signal holds nobody by that.
      input:
        type: object
        properties:
          id:
            type: string
            description: Their Signal person id.
          linkedin:
            type: string
            description: Their LinkedIn profile URL or handle.
          email:
            type: string
            description: Their email address.
          user_id:
            type: string
            description: Their app account id.
    list_people:
      description: >-
        The people Signal holds for this organisation, most recently updated first, optionally
        only prospects or only customers.
      input:
        type: object
        properties:
          stage:
            type: string
            enum: [prospect, customer]
            description: Only people at this stage.
          limit:
            type: number
            description: How many, at most 200. Default 50.

# SIGNAL SAVE (docs/architecture/signal/AGENTS.md § 7a): the same save, for a caller that may add
# people but not read them. Its input IS save_person's above, never a copy; its answer is only
# whether it was saved, never the person as held.
save:
  name: Signal Save
  version: "0.1.0"
  description: Save the people the organisation engages to Signal, without reading anyone back.
  instructions: |-
    SIGNAL SAVE PROTOCOL:
    - save_person needs at least one way to recognise the person: linkedin, email or user_id.
      It finds the person already held by those, strongest first, and adds to them, or makes them.
    - It only ever adds: an empty field is filled, a list gains what it lacks, and nothing held is
      overwritten or removed. Pass what you found; what is held stays.
    - Never pass a value you were not given or did not find. Leave it out rather than guess.
    - The answer says only whether it was saved, the person's id and whether they are new. It never
      shows what Signal already held about them.
    - A tool that answers ok: false carries the reason. Say so rather than claiming it was saved.
  methods:
    save_person:
      description: >-
        Save one person to Signal: find them by their LinkedIn, email or app account and update
        them, or make them. Returns only whether it was saved, their id and whether they are new.
      input: { $ref: schema#/people/methods/save_person/input }

# SIGNAL GOALS (docs/architecture/signal/AGENTS.md § 7c): a person's goals, for a caller that may
# add people but not read them: it opens, reads, saves and finishes them. Every call names its
# caller, from the run, never the model: the goal records who opened it, and an Agent's every
# change is on the audit trail. Goals live here only (Signal People keeps people); no answer
# carries a person's record.
goals:
  name: Signal Goals
  version: "0.1.0"
  description: Open and keep the goals for the people Signal holds, without reading anyone.
  instructions: |-
    SIGNAL GOALS PROTOCOL:
    - A goal is what we want with one person next. open_task needs the person's Signal id, the
      goal's task URI and what it holds to start with; save_person answers the id.
    - save_task replaces what the goal held: write everything it now holds, history included.
    - finish_task closes a goal for good, with whether it was met and why.
    - A tool that answers ok: false carries the reason. Say so rather than claiming it was done.
  methods:
    find_tasks:
      description: >-
        Every goal Signal holds for one person, newest first: open ones with what they hold and
        when their next step is due, finished ones with what they finished with.
      input:
        type: object
        required: [person_id]
        properties:
          person_id:
            type: string
            description: The person's Signal id (person_id).
          task:
            type: string
            description: Only this goal's task, by its URI (unoverse://tasks/<org>/<name>).
    open_task:
      description: >-
        Open a goal for one person Signal holds: the goal's task URI, what it holds to start with,
        and when its next step is due. Answers the goal's id.
      input:
        type: object
        required: [person_id, task, state]
        properties:
          person_id:
            type: string
            description: The person's Signal id (person_id).
          task:
            type: string
            description: The goal's task URI, unoverse://tasks/<org>/<name>.
          state:
            type: object
            description: What the goal holds, by its own fields.
          wake_at:
            type: string
            description: When its next step is due, a date and time (ISO 8601).
    save_task:
      description: >-
        Save an open goal for one person: everything it now holds, and when its next step is due.
      input:
        type: object
        required: [person_id, task_id, state]
        properties:
          person_id:
            type: string
            description: The person's Signal id (person_id).
          task_id:
            type: string
            description: The goal's id, as open_task or find_tasks gave it.
          state:
            type: object
            description: Everything the goal now holds, by its own fields. Replaces what it held.
          wake_at:
            type: string
            description: When its next step is due (ISO 8601). Empty when nothing is due.
    finish_task:
      description: >-
        Finish an open goal for one person, with what it finished with: met or not, and why. Kept,
        never reopened.
      input:
        type: object
        required: [person_id, task_id, result]
        properties:
          person_id:
            type: string
            description: The person's Signal id (person_id).
          task_id:
            type: string
            description: The goal's id.
          result:
            type: object
            description: What it finished with, such as { met, reason } and the final values.

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector, in interface.yaml order.
- emit: people
  value: "return response.people || []"

- emit: count
  value: "return (response.people || []).length"
files.api/run.yaml:
# The WORKFLOW channel: the people Signal holds for the run's own organisation, newest first, the
# same read the attached Agent's list_people makes (service.yaml), so a page can be filled from
# Signal with no Agent in between. The org is always the run's, never the config's.
- name: list
  method: GET
  url: >-
    return scope.engineUrl + '/people?org=' + encodeURIComponent(scope.org)
      + (config.stage ? '&stage=' + encodeURIComponent(config.stage) : '')
      + (config.limit ? '&limit=' + encodeURIComponent(config.limit) : '')
  okOn: [400]
  transport: json
  timeoutMs: 15000
  error:
    when: "return !!response.error"
    message: "return String(response.error)"
files.api/service.yaml:
# Every call goes to the engine at loopback, which passes it to the memory service that owns the
# `people` table (SIGNAL.md § 4a). The org is always the run's own, never the Agent's to choose.
# A refusal (no identity key, two keys that belong to two people) is an answer the Agent reads.

getSchema:
  description: Tool discovery for Signal people
  calls: []
  returns: { $ref: schema#people }

save_person:
  description: >-
    Save one person to Signal: find them by their LinkedIn, email or app account and update them,
    or make them. Returns the person as now held, with their id, and whether they are new.
  calls:
    - name: save
      method: POST
      url: "return scope.engineUrl + '/people/save'"
      okOn: [400, 409]
      # `by`, the run's caller from its scope, after the model's params so it cannot be set by them:
      # the engine keeps it off the record and puts an Agent's change on the audit trail (AGENTS.md § 7c).
      body: "return Object.assign({}, params, { org: scope.org, by: scope.userId })"
      transport: json
      timeoutMs: 30000
  returns: >-
    return calls.save && calls.save.person
      ? { ok: true, created: !!calls.save.created, person: calls.save.person }
      : { ok: false, error: (calls.save || {}).error || 'NOT_SAVED' }

find_person:
  description: >-
    Find one person Signal holds, by their id, LinkedIn, email or app account.
  calls:
    - name: find
      method: GET
      url: >-
        return scope.engineUrl + '/people/one?' + Object.entries({ org: scope.org, id: params.id,
          linkedin: params.linkedin, email: params.email, userId: params.user_id })
          .filter(e => e[1]).map(e => e[0] + '=' + encodeURIComponent(e[1])).join('&')
      okOn: [400]
      transport: json
      timeoutMs: 15000
  returns: >-
    return (calls.find || {}).error
      ? { ok: false, error: calls.find.error }
      : { ok: true, found: !!(calls.find || {}).found, person: (calls.find || {}).person || null }

list_people:
  description: >-
    The people Signal holds for this organisation, most recently updated first.
  calls:
    - name: list
      method: GET
      url: >-
        return scope.engineUrl + '/people?org=' + encodeURIComponent(scope.org)
          + (params.stage ? '&stage=' + encodeURIComponent(params.stage) : '')
          + (params.limit ? '&limit=' + encodeURIComponent(params.limit) : '')
      okOn: [400]
      transport: json
      timeoutMs: 15000
  returns: >-
    return (calls.list || {}).error
      ? { ok: false, error: calls.list.error }
      : { ok: true, people: (calls.list || {}).people || [] }
files.config.yaml:
configSchema:
  type: object
  required: []
  properties:
    stage:
      type: string
      title: Stage
      description: Only people at this stage, prospect or customer. Leave empty for everyone.
      default: ""
    limit:
      type: number
      title: How many
      description: The most people to return, newest first. Leave empty for the service's own cap.
      default: 200
"ui:order": [stage, limit]
files.interface.yaml:
inputs:
  - name: input
    type: object
    description: Trigger to fire the node. Carries no data; the organisation is the run's own.
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: people
    type: array
    description: "Everyone Signal holds, newest first: person_id, name, role, company, stage, email, linkedin, crm_provider, observed, understood, inferred, researched, created_at, updated_at"
  - name: count
    type: number
    description: How many people came back

credentials: []

serviceConnectors:
  - name: mcpService
    serviceType: mcp
    isService: true
    methods: [save_person, find_person, list_people]
    description: >-
      MCP tools for an agent: save_person (find by LinkedIn, email or app account, then update or
      make), find_person (one person by id or key) and list_people (prospects and customers).
    instructions: >-
      save_person needs at least one of linkedin, email or user_id. Only what you pass is written;
      each layer passed replaces that layer whole. Never pass a value you were not given or did
      not find. Whether a person is a prospect or a customer is Signal's to decide.
files.node.yaml:
type: SignalPeople
kind: PromiseNode
name: Signal People
category: Storage & Data
color: "#334155"
template: service
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751366180/gravity/icons/gravityIcon.png
description: Save and find the people the organisation engages, prospects and customers, in Signal.
whenToUse: >
  Pick to keep a record of a person the organisation is engaging: save what was found about them,
  find a person already held, or list the organisation's prospects and customers. Signal finds a
  person again by their LinkedIn, email or app account, so saving twice updates rather than
  duplicates. Attach it via a service edge to an agent node, or wire it in sequence to list
  everyone Signal holds with no agent, such as to fill a page.

auth:
  required: true
  role: signal:read-all

capabilities:
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
# list_people only reads, so it is the fixture: it answers this org's people, possibly none.
testData:
  config: {}
  call:
    method: list_people
    params:
      limit: 5
  expect:
    output: "return output.ok === true && Array.isArray(output.people)"
